title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Letter to Tate, May 1966, chapter on crystals, §2.4-2.8). A is an abelian scheme (here mostly an elliptic scheme) over S. G(A) = G(A/S) is the smooth group scheme from the previous page. In modern terms it is the universal vector extension E(A*) of the dual abelian scheme, 0 -> ω_A -> E -> A* -> 0 (up to the duality convention). Its Lie algebra is H^1_DR(A/S) or its dual, with the Hodge filtration as the canonical vector subgroup. The assertions 1º-3º being tested are:
- 1º: for any infinitesimal thickening S ⊂ T and lifting B of A to T, G(B/T) depends canonically only on A, i.e. G(A) is a crystal in groups and H^1_DR is a crystal of modules.
- 3º: liftings of A are classified by liftings of the Hodge filtration, giving a Grothendieck-Messing type theorem.

Positive results claimed:
- (a) In characteristic 0, 1º and 3º hold in the form using G(A). This is the analytic or characteristic-0 Gauss-Manin situation, where crystals coincide with modules with integrable connection.
- (b) In any characteristic, G(A) has no infinitesimal automorphisms. Reason: Hom(E, V) = 0 for any vector group V, because Hom(ω, V) ≅ Ext(A*, V) by universality and Hom(A*, V) = 0. Hence an isomorphism G(B) ≅ G(B'), if it exists, is unique. So if 1º holds for all liftings over opens U, the G(B) glue to a crystal in groups. A fortiori H(B) = Lie gives a crystal of modules. G(A) and H^1_DR(A/S) then acquire canonical absolute stratifications, functorial in A and compatible with base change. This is the standard rigidity-implies-descent argument.
- (c) 1º-3º hold for first-order liftings, at least for T = D(J), the dual-number scheme of a quasi-coherent J. This is the Kodaira-Spencer / square-zero case; in modern terms the trivial divided powers on a square-zero ideal make it a special case of Mazur-Messing.

2.7 retracts the conjectures, giving a no-go theorem. Let k have characteristic p > 0. There is no stratification relative to k (Grothendieck stratification, i.e. a crystal on the infinitesimal site, with no divided powers) on H^1_DR(A/S) that is functorial in A and compatible with base change for all elliptic A over curves S of finite type over k.

Proof sketch:
- Base change by Frobenius plus functoriality applied to the relative Frobenius A -> A^(p) make V: M^(p) -> M, with M = H^1_DR(A/S), horizontal for the stratification.
- A stratification trivializes M over the formal neighbourhood of s, M^ ≅ M_s ⊗ Ô_{S,s}, and horizontal maps become constant.
- So if A_s is supersingular (Hasse invariant 0, i.e. F^2 = 0 on H^1_DR(A_s)), the same holds on the formal neighbourhood, hence on the whole component.
- This contradicts the modular (e.g. Legendre) family, whose Hasse invariant is generically nonzero.

The next page draws the moral: only isocrystals (inverting p and working over W) can work, possibly with an overconvergence-type relaxation suggested by Washnitzer-Monsky. It also conjectures that the lifting-independence of G(B) holds exactly for ordinary abelian varieties, in line with Serre-Tate canonical lifts.
errors: The 2.7 argument genuinely needs full stratifications (all infinitesimal orders) and not just a connection. In characteristic p, Frobenius is horizontal for the Gauss-Manin connection (Katz) with no contradiction, because the p-curvature is nonzero (nilpotent) and a connection does not integrate to the formal neighbourhood. The text says 'stratification', so it is correct, but this is exactly where divided powers enter: crystalline H^1 is a crystal for PD-thickenings, which the argument does not exclude.
Compatibility with base change along Frobenius is only k-linear if k = F_p, or with a twist via relative Frobenius over k. This is a minor imprecision that is harmless if one takes k = F_p.

Claim (b) is correct, since Hom(E(A), vector group) = 0 in all characteristics. The marginal 'faux' next to b) probably refers to the conditional conclusion (existence of stratifications), which 2.7 refutes, not to the rigidity statement.
Claim (c) is true. In modern terms, square-zero ideals carry trivial divided powers, so it follows from Mazur-Messing. The marginal 'à vérifier' doubt is unnecessary.

ideas.what: Universal vector extension G(A) as the group-scheme refinement of H^1_DR; crystal in groups whose Lie algebra is the de Rham crystal
ideas.modern_name: universal vectorial extension / crystalline nature of E(A) (Mazur-Messing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Montreal 1970, Barsotti-Tate groups and Dieudonné crystals); Mazur-Messing 1974; Messing 1972
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970); ICM 1970 talk

ideas.what: Rigidity: no infinitesimal automorphisms of G(A), so uniqueness of isomorphisms gives gluing into a crystal
First-order deformations of abelian schemes classified by lifts of the Hodge filtration
No-go: H^1_DR of elliptic curves in char p admits no functorial (non-PD) stratification relative to k, via horizontality of Frobenius and the Hasse invariant
ideas.modern_name: failure of de Rham cohomology to be a crystal on the infinitesimal site in char p; necessity of divided powers / isocrystals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motivation for crystalline cohomology, Berthelot thesis)
ideas.where_published: Possibly remarked in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); unsure whether the Hasse-invariant argument appears there

missed.claim: An explicit, clean impossibility proof: horizontality of Frobenius for a hypothetical stratification would force the supersingular locus to be open. This is a concrete witness that non-PD crystals fail in char p. It is well known in spirit but rarely stated in this form in the literature.
missed.quote: Si alors s∈S est un point correspondant à un A_s de Hasse nul ... la même propriété serait vraie aux points voisins de s, ce qui est évidemment faux p.ex. pour la famille modulaire.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a neat pedagogical/historical document of why crystalline (PD) and isocrystal theories were forced. It also links to later results identifying stratified (F-divided) bundles with infinite Frobenius descent (Gieseker, dos Santos), which are incompatible with varying Hasse invariant.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (universal extension as a crystal, char-0 Gauss-Manin, first-order case, need for divided powers or isocrystals) are all well established and credited to Grothendieck/Messing/Mazur/Berthelot. The Tate letter itself is known and circulated. The Hasse-invariant no-go argument is a nice explicit historical detail but not new mathematics to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 of b): the insertion above 'infinitésimaux' is 'donnés'; the correction 'l'assertion' -> 'l'hypothèse' and 'vrai' -> 'vérifiée' are correctly read.
'postullées' is a typo corrected to 'postulées'; 'hyppthèse' to 'hypothèse'.

Margin readings are uncertain. Next to b) the word is probably 'faux'. Next to c) something like 'à vérifier, i.e. pas clair [?]'. The circled note at 2.7 reads roughly '... SO!'. All are illegible in part.
'de dimension ≤1': the ≤1 has a handwritten slash/insertion mark, possibly a correction to the dimension condition.
